data.title: M&A News: Instacart Stock (CART) Jumps 10% on Takeover Rumors
data.description:
Instacart's (CART) stock closed 10% higher on Oct. 23 as rumors of a takeover swirl around the company. Multiple media reports say that the grocery-delivery company is exploring a sale and has had held preliminary discussions with rivals Uber (UBER) and DoorDash (DASH) about a potential takeover.

Instacart, also known as Maplebear, is currently valued at about $12 billion and is reportedly working with an investment bank to evaluate its options, according to media reports. A typical takeover premium of 30% to 40% would put its valuation at as much as $17 billion, though discussions reportedly are in the preliminary stages and no deal has been announced.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Bitcoin (BTC) Grinds Lower As Market Selloff Worsens
data.description:
Bitcoin (BTC) slid lower on Oct. 23 as the selloff in stocks worsened and spread to most sectors of the market. BTC was down 0.30% at $81,250 at the end of the trading session for equity markets. The largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization is down 5% in October as volatility intensifies and investors head for the safety of government Treasury bonds.

The drop in Bitcoin on Oct. 23 comes on a day when the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 652 points lower and a day after the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite dropped nearly 700 points on Oct. 22. A growing number of issues are impacting risk assets such as technology stocks and cryptocurrencies, including worries about the artificial intelligence (AI) trade, oil prices, and bond yields.

data.description:

News That Moved the Stock Market Today

  • Brent crude oil (BZ) climbed 3.5% to a five-month high of $117 per barrel as the U.S. and Iran prepare for a return to action. The U.S. is deploying additional troops and military equipment to the Middle East as Iran threatens to target energy infrastructure, airports, and U.S. military bases across the region if Washington and Israel resume attacks, according to the Wall Street Journal.
  • U.S. Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said the U.S.-Iran war could last another year if Iran refuses to come to the negotiating table. "I'm not going to put out hypotheticals," he told the Financial Times. "One would hope that they'll come to the table in a meaningful way before that."
  • Long-dated Treasury yields resumed their uptrend following a selloff on Thursday. The 10-year yield rose 4.4 basis points (bps) to 4.99%, while the 30-year yield climbed 3.8 bps to 5.32%.
  • The University of Michigan's Index of Consumer Sentiment for October came in at 48.0, topping the estimate of 46.3 but slipping slightly from 48.1 in September. The reading remains at a five-month low as concerns over affordability and the economic outlook persist. Furthermore, year-ahead inflation expectations climbed to 4.7% from 4.6% in September, while long-term expectations increased to 3.5% from 3.4%.
  • Apple (AAPL) briefly overtook Nvidia (NVDA) in intraday trading to become the world's most valuable publicly traded company by market capitalization. That came after NVDA stock received a rare "Sell" rating from Seaport Research.
  • American Express (AXP) CEO Steve Squeri said that the company will cut approximately 5% of its global workforce to "take advantage of AI in the coming quarters and the coming years."
  • Several companies will report their earnings next week, including Microsoft (MSFT), Visa (V), Alphabet (GOOGL), and Starbucks (SBUX). Furthermore, the Fed will announce its interest rate decision on Wednesday, October 28.

A potential deal could be worth billions of dollars and provide Crown Castle with a major new source of revenue. data.title: IREN Stock: Why Analysts Still See Over 200% Upside Despite This Week's Plunge
data.description:
IREN Limited shares (IREN) sold off this week, down more than 21% in the past five days alone. This came amid fresh concerns about high borrowing costs in the neocloud and larger tech industry. Still, the analyst consensus rating on IREN stock suggests about 228% upside. Analysts have pointed to the company's customer deals, stronger GPU leasing pricing, and power portfolio.

What Are IREN Bulls Saying?

Notably, four-star JPMorgan analyst Richard Choe recently upgraded IREN stock from Sell to Buy. Choe lifted his price target from $46 to $65, suggesting 155% upside.

The analyst noted that IREN's recent deals and AI push have helped it become "a formidable neocloud" company. He also noted that the company now gets "substantially" better deals for its GPU and power capacity. For instance, Choe noted that IREN's AI cloud contracts have gone from $10-$15/W to $15-20/W or higher.

Similarly,  BTIG's five-star analyst Gregory Lewis recently reaffirmed his Buy rating on IREN. He also set a price target of $80, suggesting about 214% upside. Lewis noted that IREN stands out with its 5 gigawatts of potential power capacity.

The analyst believes that IREN's control of its supply chain makes its potential power capacity unique compared to its peers. IREN secures land, builds data centers, secures power, and even purchases GPU capacity and other hardware for its facilities.

Why Some Analysts Remain Cautious

Meanwhile, a few analysts have decided to tread cautiously on IREN shares. For instance, Jones Trading analyst Kevin Dede rated IREN stock a Hold. The analyst noted that he finds a few factors about IREN "polarizing." For example, the analyst argued that IREN has a broad customer base but lower-quality customers.

Similarly, Rothschild & Co. Redburn analyst Alexander Haissl also issued a Hold rating on IREN shares. At the current price, Haissl believes investors have sufficiently priced in IREN's risk and likely returns.

Is IREN a Good Stock to Buy Now?

On Wall Street, analysts now rate IREN's shares a Strong Buy. This consensus reflects eight Buys and two Holds assigned over the past three months.

In addition, the average IREN price target of $82.56 implies about 228% upside ahead (see IREN stock forecast here).

data.title: Could Skydance Be Bigger Than Disney? Skydance (NYSE:SKYD) Stock Rises
data.description:
Entertainment giant Skydance (SKYD) could be bigger than Disney (DIS), or even bigger than Netflix (NFLX) thanks to its recently concluded merger deal. JPMorgan analysts actually gave Skydance stock an upgrade, taking it from Underweight to Neutral, though they also dialed back the price target. Skydance stock rose fractionally in the closing minutes of Friday's trading. Skydance has seen a 53.41% loss in its share price over the past year.

Bigger Than You Might Expect

JPMorgan recently restarted coverage of Skydance, now that it is no longer either Paramount Skydance or Warner Bros. Discovery. The rating change was one thing, but JPMorgan lowered the price target from a previous level of $14 per share down to $9 per share.

The thesis behind this is that Skydance will see cost-saving opportunities as a result of the merger, as well as new opportunities to expand its presence in streaming. There will be more room for content monetization, as well as cross-selling of its streaming services, though the combination of the two services—HBO Max and Paramount+—may render that something of a moot point. Also, the combined firm will have the ability to remove some duplicated cost, though this may mean quite a few lost jobs.

Wiseman Out

Meanwhile Skydance will be operating on something like a back foot as the Paramount+ head of originals, Jane Wiseman, is leaving the company. It turns out that Wiseman's position may have been one of those "duplicated costs" we heard about previously. The new co-CEO and chief content officer for Skydance's direct-to-consumer operation, Casey Bloys, revealed that much of his original team from HBO will stay in their current positions.

Perhaps the most galling part of this is contained in Bloys' memo about the transition, where he said, "I also want to thank Jane Wiseman. Jane, in her partnership with Cindy Holland, has done amazing work at Paramount+. The development slate is incredibly impressive, and Jane has graciously offered to help with the transition. She is an extraordinarily talented executive. I appreciate all her support and wish her all the best." "Extraordinarily talented"…but not talented enough to keep, then?

data.title: Robinhood Stock (HOOD) Options Traders Are Pricing a 10.26% Earnings Swing
data.description:
Robinhood Markets (HOOD) is expected to report third-quarter earnings after the market closes on October 27, 2026. The October 30, 2026 options expiration implies a 10.26%, or $9.75, move in either direction. With shares trading at $95.05, the nearest strike is $95, where the call costs $5.10 and the put costs $4.65. Therefore:

  • ATM straddle = $5.10 + $4.65 = $9.75
  • Implied dollar move = $9.75
  • Implied percentage move = $9.75 ÷ $95.05 × 100 = 10.26%
  • Upper bound = $95.05 + $9.75 = $104.80
  • Lower bound = $95.05 − $9.75 = $85.30
data.author: Vince Condarcuri

data.title: Why Did Analysts Slash Bloom Energy Stock (BE) Price Targets Despite Praising Q3 Earnings Beats?
data.description:
Bloom Energy (BE) stock sank 11% on Friday after the company's Q3 earnings report acted as a catalyst for analyst price target cuts for BE shares.

Here's how some of the top-ranked analysts on TipRanks adjusted their BE stock price targets after earnings.

  • J.P. Morgan analyst Mark Strouse lowered his BE stock price target to $292 from $314 and maintained a Buy rating. His price target suggests a possible 50.52% upside for the shares.
  • Roth MKM Chip Moore cut his price target to $230 from $260 and stuck with a Hold rating. The analyst's new price target implies an 18.56% upside for the stock.
  • BTIG analyst Gregory Lewis reduced his price target to $250 from $295 and kept a Buy rating. This new price target represents a 28.87% upside for BE.

Analysts were cautious with Bloom Energy despite a strong earnings report. The company's adjusted EPS of 94 cents and revenue of $1.24 billion both easily surpassed Wall Street's estimates of 69 cents per share and $1.07 billion in revenue.

Promotion

Bloom Energy also updated its 2026 guidance ranges to adjusted EPS of $3.10 to $3.40 and revenue of $4.4 billion to $4.6 billion. At midpoints of $3.25 per share and revenue of $4.5 billion, the company is on track to smash analysts' estimates of $3.14 per share and revenue of $4.38 billion.

So What's Behind the BE Stock Price Target Cuts Today?

While J.P. Morgan analyst Strouse said that Bloom Energy "continues to impress," he still cut his price target. However, the analyst said this had more to do with lower trading multiples in the company's peer group.

As for Roth MKM analyst Moore, he pointed to multiple contractions as the reason for his BE stock price cut. That's despite what the analyst called "another quarter of very impressive results."

Moving onto BTIG analyst Lewis, he highlighted near-term margin drag connected to the ramp of new production capacity and expedited customer timelines as reasons for his price cut. Even so, he noted that Bloom Energy is in the prime position to deliver behind-the-meter (BTM) generation capacity that is high in demand.

Where Does Wall Street Stand on BE Stock After Earnings?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus for Bloom Energy is Moderate Buy, based on 10 Buy and 10 Hold ratings over the past three months. With that comes an average BE stock price target of $291.50, representing a potential 51.08% upside for the shares. (See BE Stock Forecast)
